But that is not what he did. Ballas took one look at her that evening, and... he was stricken, Drifter. Positively and absolutely beside himself.
I had never seen anything like it. It was as though no one else in the room even existed, save for Margulis. He seemed even... somehow too shy to speak to her. Him! Ballas!
Really?
You're making this up.
I swear on whatever remains of my honor! And what reason would I have to lie? What do I care of your opinion of the validity of their relationship?
I swear on whatever remains of my honor I am not! And what reason would I have to lie? What do I care of your opinion of the validity of their relationship?
It simply saddens me that you lot would so quickly simplify something that is decidedly far more complicated than you would have it.
They were in love, whether you wish to believe it or not. Ballas eshewed all class rules and tradition to take as his lover - and his sole romantic companion - an Archimedean.
Only true love could have sent a man so spectacularly mad as it sent him, when it all went so very wrong...
How do you figure? Wasn't he responsible for her death?
Ballas was the one who had her executed.

First, let us assume all you know is correct, and that his actions there were purely of his own accord. Let us assume that there were no other political maneuverings or blackmail or anything else being done behind the scenes that may have forced his hand.
Even if that were to be the case, and Ballas called for her execution entirely without influence, consider that it was already too late. The betrayal he felt had already cleaved him in two.
His heart and his mind was already broken.
I am not going to start feeling bad for him, if that's what you're asking me to do.
Because of the Tenno? Or because of what they did to her?
I am not asking you to have anything of the sort! Ballas deserves anything but whatever piss you can spare to spend on wherever you buried his corpse - if he even has a grave.

In a way, both. And in a way, neither. He was driven to madness that day, when he called for her execution. In fact, I would not be surprised if some part of him did not entirely recall doing the deed.
I am merely stating that on the day he called for her execution, he was a madman. I would not be surprised if some part of him did not entirely recall doing the deed, after the fact.

Ballas loved Margulis. With his whole person, completely - entirely devoted to her. He would have sacrificed anything and everything for her. His soul, his body, the Orokin Empire. Anything you could possibly dream of.

No cost was too great. No morals worth sacrificing. If you had handed him a newborn babe and told him Margulis wished its brains dashed out upon the rocks, it would be dead before you finished your sentence.
He would have burned the Origin System to ashes and rebuilt it in her image, Usurper... but herein lies the tragedy.
Margulis? Aah, Margulis. Dear, sweet, darling Margulis... she still had a conscience.
And when she saw the poor Tenno, the poor, Void-torn children...
Something in her life was more important than Ballas. Something in her life was worth sacrificing her life for... that was not him.
That was not her love for him.

And he knew this, my sweet Drifter. He knew this from the moment she laid her eyes on them. And it was driven home when her "mad animals" ensured they were the last she ever saw. Or at least that was what the rumors were amongst us Orokin.
Can you imagine the joy amongst the Orokin? Seeing Ballas' precious Archimedean's Void-torn, rabid brats burn out her eyes?
But I think, it was before then, at the precise moment Margulis fought to save the Tenno that Ballas's heart shattered into a thousand pieces, and never recovered.
